# Google Trends

Day 2, 16:20 · Omri Weisman, Engineering Manager, Google Trends · coverage: transcript

Speaker matched from his self-introduction to the official speaker list. No slides were photographed.

## Claims

- **[Stage]** Google Trends is a free Google tool that gives access to a sample of aggregated, anonymized and categorized searches.
  <br><sub>`D2-C747` · Day 2, Google Trends (Omri Weisman) · confirmed by Google docs · [Get started with Google Trends](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/monitor-debug/trends-start), [FAQ about Google Trends data](https://support.google.com/trends/answer/4365533?hl=en), [Basics of Google Trends](https://newsinitiative.withgoogle.com/resources/trainings/basics-of-google-trends/)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google Trends data covers searches on Google Search, including web, image, shopping and news search, plus searches on YouTube.
  <br><sub>`D2-C748` · Day 2, Google Trends (Omri Weisman) · confirmed by Google docs · [Compare search terms and topics](https://support.google.com/trends/answer/17309543?hl=en), [Get started with Google Trends](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/monitor-debug/trends-start)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google Discover is not included in Google Trends, because Discover is a content feed with no search box, while Trends counts only the queries people type into Google Search or YouTube.
  <br><sub>`D2-C749` · Day 2, Google Trends (Omri Weisman) · consistent with Google docs · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover), [Compare search terms and topics](https://support.google.com/trends/answer/17309543?hl=en)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Trends FAQ says Google Trends filters out searches made by Google products and services, including the internal searches made by AI Mode and AI Overviews.
  > "This includes internal searches made by AI Mode and AI Overviews."
  <br><sub>`D2-C750` · Google Trends Help · annotates Day 2, Google Trends · is the documentation · [FAQ about Google Trends data](https://support.google.com/trends/answer/4365533?hl=en)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google Trends cannot show demand that reaches people through the Discover feed, so Discover visibility has to be judged from Search Console's Discover performance report rather than from Trends.
  <br><sub>`D2-C751` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Google Trends</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google handles more than five trillion searches a year, a figure Google announced publicly at the beginning of 2025.
  <br><sub>`D2-C752` · Day 2, Google Trends (Omri Weisman) · confirmed by Google docs · [AI, personalization and the future of shopping](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/ai-personalization-and-the-future-of-shopping/) · Repeats [D1-C006](D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** By the author's arithmetic, more than five trillion Google searches a year means on average more than 13.7 billion searches a day, or roughly 160,000 a second.
  <br><sub>`D2-C753` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Google Trends</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google Trends data can be viewed for the whole world, for a single country or for a region within a country, for example Spain or Catalonia.

- **[Stage]** Google said Google Trends data is almost real time, reaching up to a few minutes before the moment of viewing.

- **[Analysis]** Before treating a spike in an ambiguous keyword as demand for your topic, zoom in on the period in Google Trends and check the commonly searched queries, since another meaning of the word (as with 'ai' in 2012) may be driving it.

  <br><sub>`D2-C783` · Day 2, Google Trends (Omri Weisman) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google Trends shows search interest, not search volume: each point on its 0 to 100 scale represents the share of searches for the term out of all searches.
  > "Search interest is not search volume."
  <br><sub>`D2-C784` · Day 2, Google Trends (Omri Weisman) · confirmed by Google docs · [FAQ about Google Trends data](https://support.google.com/trends/answer/4365533?hl=en), [Basics of Google Trends](https://newsinitiative.withgoogle.com/resources/trainings/basics-of-google-trends/) · Used by the glossary term *Search interest*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Because total Google searches were far fewer in 2004 than today, a falling search interest share in Google Trends can hide a rising number of searches.
  <br><sub>`D2-C785` · Day 2, Google Trends (Omri Weisman) · consistent with Google docs · [FAQ about Google Trends data](https://support.google.com/trends/answer/4365533?hl=en), [Basics of Google Trends](https://newsinitiative.withgoogle.com/resources/trainings/basics-of-google-trends/)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said its internal numbers show the actual volume of ski-related searches is going up, even though ski's share of all searches in Google Trends has declined since 2004.

  <br><sub>`D2-C786` · Day 2, Google Trends (Omri Weisman) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google stressed that the difference between search interest and search volume matters most when reading very long time ranges in Google Trends.

- **[Analysis]** A Google Trends line that falls over many years is not proof that a market is shrinking; compare terms against each other in the same chart, and take absolute numbers from keyword tools or Search Console impressions.

- **[Stage]** Google presented three uses of Google Trends for content creation, marketing and SEO: keyword selection, scheduling and ideation.
  <br><sub>`D2-C789` · Day 2, Google Trends (Omri Weisman) · consistent with Google docs · [Get started with Google Trends](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/monitor-debug/trends-start) · Extended by [D3-C104](D3-S04-lightning-session-k-facets-of-quality.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** For keyword selection, Google recommended entering candidate keywords on the Google Trends Explore page, setting the relevant country, region and time frame, and seeing which terms have the higher search interest.
